title: Lecture 11 Boss Problems
subtitle: Boolean operators, bool, and input validation

leap.starter:
year = int(input('Year: '))
# Report whether the year is a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 2024
cases.expected: Year: 2024 is a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 2023
cases.expected: Year: 2023 is not a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 1900
cases.expected: Year: 1900 is not a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 2000
cases.expected: Year: 2000 is a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 2100
cases.expected: Year: 2100 is not a leap year.

cases.name: Typed 1600
cases.expected: Year: 1600 is a leap year.

leap.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*(import|from)\b", __code__, re.M), "No imports. Everything here can be done with if statements and arithmetic."
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*if\b", __code__, re.M)) == 1 and re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Use exactly one if with an else."
assert not re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "No elif here. One condition built with and/or covers every case."
assert re.search(r"\band\b", __code__) and re.search(r"\bor\b", __code__), "Combine the three divisibility tests with and and or."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % to test divisibility."
assert len(__stdout__.strip().splitlines()) == 1, "Print one line."
hints: A year is a leap year when it is divisible by 4, except that a year divisible by 100 is not, unless it is also divisible by 400. Turn each 'divisible by' into a `%` test and join them with `and` and `or`. Brackets decide which pair is joined first.
leap.answerNote: The brackets matter: the year must be divisible by 4, and then it must either miss 100 or hit 400. Without them, and binds before or and 1900 comes out as a leap year.

plate.starter:
plate = input('Plate: ')
# Say whether the plate is old style, new style, or not valid.

cases.name: Typed ABC123
cases.expected: Plate: ABC123 is an old style plate.

cases.name: Typed 1234ABC
cases.expected: Plate: 1234ABC is a new style plate.

cases.name: Typed abc123
cases.expected: Plate: abc123 is not a valid plate.

cases.name: Typed ABC12
cases.expected: Plate: ABC12 is not a valid plate.

cases.name: Typed 1234abc
cases.expected: Plate: 1234abc is not a valid plate.

cases.name: Typed 123ABCD
cases.expected: Plate: 123ABCD is not a valid plate.

cases.name: Typed A1B2C3
cases.expected: Plate: A1B2C3 is not a valid plate.

cases.name: Typed 12345AB
cases.expected: Plate: 12345AB is not a valid plate.

plate.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*(import|from)\b", __code__, re.M), "No imports. Everything here can be done with if statements and arithmetic."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M) and re.search(r"^\s*else\s*:", __code__, re.M), "Use an if/elif/else chain: old style, new style, not valid."
assert "len(" in __code__, "Check the length first with len()."
assert ".isalpha()" in __code__ and ".isupper()" in __code__ and ".isdigit()" in __code__, "Use isalpha(), isupper() and isdigit() on the letter part and the digit part."
assert "[" in __code__, "Use slices to pick out the letter part and the digit part."
assert re.search(r"\band\b", __code__), "Join the tests for one style with and."
assert len(__stdout__.strip().splitlines()) == 1, "Print one line."
hints: A slice like `plate[:3]` is the first three characters and `plate[3:]` is the rest. Test the length first, then each part with the string methods. `isalpha()` alone accepts lowercase letters, so add `isupper()`.
plate.answerNote: Each style is one and-chain: right length, letters where letters belong, digits where digits belong. The length test comes first so the slices line up with the right parts.

roulette.starter:
spin = input('Spin: ')
# Print every bet that pays for this spin.

cases.name: Typed 13
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 13.
Pay 13
Pay Black
Pay Odd
Pay 1 to 18

cases.name: Typed 0
cases.expected: Spin: Pay 0

cases.name: Typed 00
cases.expected: Spin: Pay 00

cases.name: Typed 1
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 1.
Pay 1
Pay Red
Pay Odd
Pay 1 to 18

cases.name: Typed 12
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 12.
Pay 12
Pay Red
Pay Even
Pay 1 to 18

cases.name: Typed 36
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 36.
Pay 36
Pay Red
Pay Even
Pay 19 to 36

cases.name: Typed 20
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 20.
Pay 20
Pay Black
Pay Even
Pay 19 to 36

cases.name: Typed 18
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 18.
Pay 18
Pay Red
Pay Even
Pay 1 to 18

cases.name: Typed 29
cases.expected:
Spin: The spin landed on 29.
Pay 29
Pay Black
Pay Odd
Pay 19 to 36

roulette.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*(import|from)\b", __code__, re.M), "No imports. Everything here can be done with if statements and arithmetic."
assert re.search(r"^spin = input\('Spin: '\)\s*$", __source__, re.M), "Keep spin as text, so that 00 stays 00. Convert to int only after ruling out 0 and 00."
assert re.search(r"\band\b", __code__) and re.search(r"\bor\b", __code__) and re.search(r"\bnot\b", __code__), "Use and, or and not to build the red test."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % to tell odd from even."
__lines__ = __stdout__.strip().splitlines()
assert len(__lines__) in (1, 5), "0 and 00 print one line; every other spin prints five."
hints: Read the spin as text and test `spin == '0' or spin == '00'` before converting. Once you know it is 1 to 36, `int(spin)` gives a number to compare.
Store `odd` and `first_group` as Boolean variables first. Red is `first_group and odd`, or `not first_group and not odd`. Then each print block is a short if/else on those names.
roulette.answerNote: The zeros are handled first, as text, so 00 never turns into 0. Naming odd and first_group turns the red rule into one readable line each, and the last three if/else blocks each print exactly one bet.

nextday.starter:
year = int(input('Year: '))
month = int(input('Month: '))
day = int(input('Day: '))
# Print the date of the following day.

cases.name: Typed 2013 11 18
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2013-11-18 is 2013-11-19.

cases.name: Typed 2013 11 30
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2013-11-30 is 2013-12-01.

cases.name: Typed 2013 12 31
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2013-12-31 is 2014-01-01.

cases.name: Typed 2024 2 28
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2024-02-28 is 2024-02-29.

cases.name: Typed 2023 2 28
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2023-02-28 is 2023-03-01.

cases.name: Typed 2024 2 29
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2024-02-29 is 2024-03-01.

cases.name: Typed 2100 2 28
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2100-02-28 is 2100-03-01.

cases.name: Typed 2000 2 28
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2000-02-28 is 2000-02-29.

cases.name: Typed 2026 1 9
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2026-01-09 is 2026-01-10.

cases.name: Typed 2026 4 30
cases.expected: Year: Month: Day: The day after 2026-04-30 is 2026-05-01.

nextday.check:
import re
assert not re.search(r"^\s*(import|from)\b", __code__, re.M), "No imports. Everything here can be done with if statements and arithmetic."
assert re.search(r"^\s*elif\b", __code__, re.M), "Use an if/elif/else chain for the number of days in the month."
assert re.search(r"\band\b", __code__) and re.search(r"\bor\b", __code__), "Use and and or for the leap year test and the 30 day months."
assert "%" in __code__, "Use % for the leap year test."
assert re.search(r":[^}]*0>?2d?\}", __source__), "Show month and day with two digits using :02d."
assert len(__stdout__.strip().splitlines()) == 1, "Print one line."
hints: First work out how many days the month has: February depends on the leap year rule from Boss 1, four months have 30, the rest have 31. An if/elif/else chain that stores `days` does it.
Add 1 to the day. If that passes `days`, the day becomes 1 and the month goes up by one. If the month passes 12, the month becomes 1 and the year goes up by one. Two separate ifs, in that order.
Keep the typed date in `year`, `month` and `day` and put the answer in new variables, so the print can show both. `{month:02d}` prints 2 as `02`.
nextday.answerNote: The month length is one chain, then two rollover ifs run in order: day into month, then month into year. New variables hold the answer so the original date is still there for the print.
